sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent infrastructure dominates today's visible GitHub Trending snapshot: Google's open orchestration runtime leads with +2,305 stars, while coding-agent applications span office productivity, video editing, tool routing, and financial-services workflows. Security remains present through a mobile-forensics toolkit.

sections.title: mvt-project/mvt
sections.description: Mobile forensics tooling for finding signs of device compromise.

sections.title: anthropics/financial-services
sections.description: Anthropic's financial-services-focused repository and workflow examples.

sections.title: dream-num/univer
sections.description: An office harness for AI agents covering spreadsheets, docs, slides, canvas, relational tables, and PDF.

sections.title: superdesigndev/treg
sections.description: An OpenRouter-style layer for agent tools.

sections.title: davila7/claude-code-templates
sections.description: A CLI tool for configuring and monitoring Claude Code.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent orchestration and substrate layers; agents embedded in work and creative software; agent tool routing and operations. Python leads with 5 of 8 listed repositories; Go has 2, and TypeScript has 1.

sections.title: Notable Shifts
sections.content: The strongest visible shift is from standalone model demos toward agent systems that orchestrate tools and operate inside concrete domains.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: GitHub's daily signal is heavily concentrated on making agents usable, governable, and domain-specific. The most consequential momentum is around orchestration infrastructure, while the fastest-growing applications turn agents into interfaces for existing work products and creative tools.
